questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Passable
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Passable"** means something that is just good enough, acceptable but not excellent. (संतोषजनक)

 
 
• **Example: **The food at the restaurant was** passable,** but nothing special.
 
 
 
• **"Inadequate" **refers to something that is not sufficient or not enough, falling short of what is required. (अपर्याप्त)
 
 
• **Example: **The resources provided were** inadequate **to complete the project successfully.
 
 

Hence, we can infer that the** opposite **of **'passable'** is **'inadequate'**.

• **Middling** (मध्यम): Of average size, quality, or extent.

 
 
• **Example:** His performance in the exam was** middling,** neither outstanding nor poor.
 
 
 
• **Particular **(विशेष): Specific or special.
 
 
• **Example: **She was very **particular **about the details of the design.
 
 
 
• **Lavish** (आलीशान): Sumptuously rich, elaborate, or luxurious.
 
 
• **Example:** They threw a** lavish** party for their wedding anniversary.

________ useful gadgets should find a home in every kitchen.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

• The subject of the sentence is** "useful gadgets,"** which is a** plural noun.**
 
• The correct demonstrative pronoun to use with plural nouns is **"these."**

• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

**Correct Sentence:** ***"These useful gadgets should find a home in every kitchen."***

• **Option 2: "This"** – Incorrect because "this" is singular and the noun "gadgets" is plural.
 
• **Option 4: "They"** – Incorrect because it does not fit the grammatical structure required in this context.
